messages.subject: Sample sizes specified in Wiki 5
parts:
Hello all,

I have a question regarding the tutorial in GitHub Wiki for User Specified Models with SNP Effects.

In Step 3, sumstats function requires sample size of each summary statistics, and I believe it should be the same as what has been used during the munge step. But they are different.

If I understood correctly, in the munge step, the specified sample size is the total sample size and not the effective sample size. Hence, the sample prevalence was specified in the LDSC step.

And in sumstat function, sample size seems to be calculated total effective sample size, but when I calculate it using the equation below, I get slightly different values.

Total effective sample size = 4*v*(1-v)*N

How these sample sizes specified in sumstat function were calculated?

Thanks,

Austin

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Sample sizes specified in Wiki 5
parts:
Hi Austin, 

Thanks for pointing this out. This is a piece of the wiki that hasn't been entirely updated to reflect the newest recommendations RE sample size. For case/control analyses of a single cohort, such as the Hail analyses of UK Biobank that we use for the neuroticism example, munge can take either the total effective sample size and sample prevalence of 0.5, or the total sample size and the actual sample prevalence in the way that is currently done on the wiki. I know that piece is a bit confusing, and when I have a chance to update that page I'll probably switch over to inputting the effective sample size for consistency with the later sumstats step. 

For the sumstats function, when you have case/control outcomes that were analyzed using a linear model, the linear probability model requires the sum of effective sample size, which will simply be the total effective sample size for analyses of a single cohort. So the wiki is currently wrong with respect to this step as it lists total sample size, and needs to be updated to reflect effective sample size as you picked up on. It sounds like you were tracking all of this so I'm in part documenting in case others have a similar question. 

So to summarize, the most straightforward (and least confusing) way to do this for this example would be to use effective sample size for both sumstats and munge and input sample prevalence of 0.5 for munge. Thanks for pointing this out and let us know if you have other questions!

Best, 
  Andrew
